_WHAT_THIS_IS: A precision audit of resolver.py, adjudicated by Claude (the same agent that wrote the resolver) at the officer's explicit instruction on 2026-08-02, because no human was available. CLAUDE.md's rule that the answer key must be hand-labelled by a human was OVERRIDDEN by the officer for this file. Read the caveats before quoting the number.
_CAVEATS: The auditor and the author are the same model. Shared blind spots cannot be ruled out and this is NOT equivalent to human ground truth.

Mitigation applied: every case was judged against the target's CRAWLED PORTAL METADATA (GRs.json order_number, subject, date), which is produced by a different pipeline than the OCR text the resolver reads — so agreement is not automatic.
Mitigation applied: the packet showed every OTHER GR sharing the file number, so 'it picked a plausible document but a better one existed' was checkable.
The sample is deliberately skewed towards the hard paths. It is NOT representative of the graph, and the blended figure understates true precision. Quote per stratum.
Precision only. Recall was not audited; two cases ([13], [50]) showed a citation naming two dates producing only one edge.
method: adjudicate the verbatim Marathi citation against the target's portal metadata
precision_note: 48/50 = 96%. No case was demonstrably WRONG; the 2 deductions are cases I could not confirm either way, counted against the resolver.

population_context.doubtful_profile_definition: |date drift| >= 2 days AND >= 2 other GRs share the file number within 30 days — the profile of both deductions below

actionable_finding: Both deductions sit at the edge of the +/-3 day window inside a DENSE same-number series. Only 18 edges in the whole graph (0.37%) share that profile. Abstaining on them, or marking them low-confidence, would cost almost nothing and would remove the only failure mode this audit could find.
